questions.q: In an on-premises ERP model, who is responsible for maintaining the servers and applying security patches?
options: No one — on-premises software patches itself
questions.explain: On-premises means the customer owns and runs the infrastructure, so its own IT department handles servers, patching, backups, and upgrades.
SaaS stands for Software as a Service — the vendor runs the application and the customer accesses it, typically through a browser, for a subscription.

questions.q: Which of these is a genuine downside of cloud (SaaS) ERP compared to on-premises?
options: There is no way to access the system remotely
The customer must buy and maintain their own servers
The customer has far less control over exactly when updates happen
Subscription costs are always higher than on-premises licensing
questions.explain: The vendor controls the update schedule in a SaaS model, trading the customer's control over upgrade timing for continuous, low-effort access to new features.

questions.q: Which two products does Oracle sell that represent the on-premises and cloud models respectively?
options: Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications for both
Oracle E-Business Suite (on-premises) and Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications (SaaS)
questions.explain: Oracle sells E-Business Suite as an on-premises product and Oracle Fusion Cloud Applications as its SaaS offering — this course focuses on the latter.

questions.q: In the cloud/SaaS model, what generally replaces deep code-level customization as the primary way to change system behavior?
options: Hiring a vendor's competitor to rewrite the code
There is no way to change behavior in SaaS
questions.explain: SaaS products are generally configuration-first: behavior is changed through setup screens and choices rather than modifying the underlying code.
